item.title: LOT-050: moderator alert (prepare, submit once, HFR's text as the answer)
item.body:
Lot: LOT-050 (moderator alert)
Closes #76
Claim: ext/francoisgn-opus-1
Author model: Opus 5.5

Supersedes #359 (taken over from moust4ki at c98a446). The lot's code and tests are those Fable approved on #359 (last APPROVE at `c98a4468`); this PR adds a merge of the current `dev-swift` (row renumbered) and one review round (`alertForm` back to five parameters for SwiftLint).

**Problem.** SwiftHFR could not report a message to the moderators. Legacy could, but:
- it showed any answer from HFR as a success;
- the Objective-C app removed emoji from the reason without saying so;
- the Swift service posted to a default address when it could not read the form's action.

**Cause.** LOT-050 had not been written. Its dependencies are merged: LOT-036 (alert form parser), LOT-037 (`.alertPrepare`), LOT-031 (the alert link) and LOT-048 (write conventions).

**Change** (spec `docs/lots/LOT-050-moderator-alert.md`):
- **`ModeratorAlertFlow.prepare(link:in:)`** (new `HFRClient/Alert/`). It does one GET of the message's alert link through the account's session. A session without a usable identity (logged out) is `notLoggedIn` before any request.
  - The link is checked first: `https` forum page, path exactly `/user/modo.php`, a single forum `cat`, `post` and `numreponse`.
  - LOT-037's `.alertPrepare` reading comes first: "already alerted" carries HFR's own sentence, never a fixed text; `R88`, the real page of a message already reported, reads so.
  - Otherwise the page must hold the LOT-036 form with `raison`, a non-empty `hash_check` (recorded in the session) and an action that names **the same message** on the forum origin.
- **`submit(reason:with:)`**:
  - a blank reason, or one with characters outside the BMP, is refused before sending (Q-3, as for posts);
  - a form read before a logout or a login of another account in the same session is refused before sending (`sessionChanged`), as `PostingForm` does since #342; a re-login of the same account still sends;
  - the form is posted in document order with CRLF, once, redirects not followed, never retried;
  - every answer with a sentence comes back as `ModeratorAlertAnswer(message:)`, neither a success nor a refusal. Only `W17c`'s logged-out sentence is read. No sentence, or a failed exchange, is `unconfirmed`.
- **Captures from #394**: HFR's success page has a back link (`W46`), so LOT-037's write rule would read it as a refusal; it comes back as HFR's text. Reading `W46` as a success, and "Vous devez être identifié…" (`R89`, `W47`) as logged out, is #395's (LOT-037's classifier). A session known to be logged out never requests the page; if HFR dropped the session anyway, `R89` reads as already alerted and `W47` as HFR's text, both with HFR's sentence, until #395.
- **Shared code**: `PostingBody` takes a named textarea (defaults unchanged for posts), and the reason's character check is LOT-096's `PostCharacterCheck.truncatingCharacters(in:)`, the one posts use. HFRParsing gains `HopFormParser.moderationLayout`.
- **Tests**: `R46`'s prepared form and its POST equal the LOT-004 oracle. `R21`'s link is `R46`'s request. Captured `.hop` pages stand in for the uncaptured shapes. 16 mutations are each caught by a test.
- No HFRModels type is added or changed. Docs: CHANGELOG-LEGACY row 66 (after `dev-swift`'s 59-65; renumbered on merge), HFR-PROTOCOL §6c `### LOT-050` (last).

Local check at the head, on Linux (Swift 6.2.4): `swift build --build-tests` and `swift test --package-path Packages/HFRKit` (1 429 tests) pass; `check-lot-deps.py` 0 violations; markdownlint 0 errors.

State-changing flow (a write to HFR). Cross-contributor review: waived by the maintainer (francoisgn, 2026-11-05) in favour of the adversarial Fable sub-agent review on the exact head.

  * Added moderator-alert preparation and submission with form validation and session checks.

comments.body:
Walkthrough

The change adds a moderator-alert flow that validates an alert link, prepares a form through an authenticated session, and submits a validated reason once. It returns HFR response text without classifying it as confirmed success. The change also adds form parsing, tests, and protocol documentation. **Changes: Moderator alert** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Alert contracts and form parsing**
`Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Alert/*`, `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Posting/PostingBody.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRParsing/Forms/HopFormLayout.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Tests/HFRParsingTests/Forms/HopFormParserTests.swift`|Adds alert target, page, form, answer, and error types. Adds moderation form layout parsing and configurable textarea and required-field validation for posting bodies.| |**Prepare an alert form**
`Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Alert/ModeratorAlertFlow.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Tests/HFRClientTests/Alert/ModeratorAlertHarness.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Tests/HFRClientTests/Alert/ModeratorAlertPrepareTests.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Tests/HFRClientTests/Session/ConcurrentLoginTokenTests.swift`|Validates alert links and sessions, fetches and classifies the page, and returns an already-alerted result or validated form. Tests cover page outcomes, request validation, and preserving a fresher session token.| |**Submit a reason and parse the response**
`Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRClient/Alert/ModeratorAlertFlow.swift`, `Packages/HFRKit/Tests/HFRClientTests/Alert/ModeratorAlertSubmitTests.swift`, `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md`, `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/lots/LOT-050-moderator-alert.md`|Validates the reason and session identity before sending one POST. Recognized logged-out responses become errors; recognized HFR text is returned without a success classification. Tests and documentation cover request fields and response handling.| **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~45 minutes ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant ModeratorAlertFlow participant HFRSession participant HFR Client->>ModeratorAlertFlow: prepare alert link ModeratorAlertFlow->>HFRSession: fetch page in selected session HFRSession->>HFR: GET alert page HFR-->>HFRSession: page response HFRSession-->>ModeratorAlertFlow: page response ModeratorAlertFlow-->>Client: already-alerted result or form Client->>ModeratorAlertFlow: submit reason with form ModeratorAlertFlow->>HFRSession: POST form once HFRSession->>HFR: submit alert HFR-->>HFRSession: response page HFRSession-->>ModeratorAlertFlow: response page ModeratorAlertFlow-->>Client: answer text or error ``` **Possibly related issues** - ezzz/HFRnow#225: The app-level moderator-alert screen depends on LOT-050 and can use this alert flow. - ezzz/HFRnow#395: Defines a later context-specific confirmation rule for the submitted HFR sentence. **Possibly related PRs** - [ezzz/HFRnow#18](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/18): Adds the `.alertPrepare` response classification used to identify already-reported messages. - [ezzz/HFRnow#315](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/315): Adds the session-token compare-and-set used during form preparation.
Merge Risk: Minimal · up to 66d52

The previously reported parameter-count failure is fixed. No remaining issue identified here needs resolution before merging.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 66d52

The new operation is narrowly scoped to a validated forum message and does not automatically retry uncertain submissions. No introduced exploitable security condition was established. Concurrent account replacement and repeated caller submissions remain limitations: the identity check is not atomic with sending, and the flow does not provide exactly-once delivery. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The new authority is an account-authenticated report concerning one selected public-forum message per prepared form. Target validation excludes private-conversation categories and binds the action to that message; the flow does not introduce moderator credentials or a general-purpose destination URL. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The caller-provided link and HTML form action must pass HTTPS forum-origin validation, use the exact alert path, and identify the same category, topic, and message through single-valued required parameters. Missing or mismatched actions fail closed rather than using a fallback. - _observed_ — Preparation follows the pre-existing session redirect policy, which permits HTTPS redirects within hardware.fr and its subdomains before the final forum-origin check. External redirects and HTTPS downgrades are blocked. This inherited policy is broader than the alert POST destination restriction; Linux cookie forwarding across followed redirects is documented. - _inferred_ — The identity check and send are separate asynchronous operations, so concurrent account replacement can interleave and change the cookies used by the POST. PostingFlow already has this pattern at the PR base. Alerts inherit that limitation, but acceptance of an original-account form token with replacement-account cookies is not established by the inspected evidence. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — The prepared form is reusable and has no consumed state. Although submit never retries internally, repeated caller invocations can issue additional POSTs, including after an unconfirmed outcome. Server-side duplicate suppression is not established, so this is not an exactly-once contract. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — If concurrent account replacement must preserve a strict local no-send guarantee, consider a shared identity-bound send operation that checks the expected identity against the credential snapshot used for the request. This would strengthen both alerts and existing posting flows; it is not evidence of a verified cross-account server action.

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+import Foundation
+import HFRModels
+import HFRNetwork
+import HFRParsing
+
+/// Reports a message to the moderators with HFR's own page and form, through the selected account's session (LOT-050,
+/// audit D5).
+///
+/// `prepare` reads the message's alert link (LOT-031): HFR either says the message was already reported or serves the
+/// form (`R46`). `submit` posts the form like a browser, once, never retried. HFR's answer to it is not read until #395,
+/// so it is never reported as a success: the app shows HFR's own sentence. The mailto fallback is the app's (LOT-135).
+public struct ModeratorAlertFlow: Sendable {
+    /// Creates the flow.
+    public init() {}
+
+    /// Fetches the alert page at `link` (`MessageActions.alertURL`) through `session`.
+    ///
+    /// A session without a usable identity (logged out, or its `md_user` expired) is `notLoggedIn` before any request:
+    /// HFR's alert page without a session (`R89`) would otherwise read as already alerted until #395.
+    ///
+    /// LOT-037's `.alertPrepare` classification comes first: a `.hop` with a link or an input is "already alerted"
+    /// (legacy rule, `AlerteModoViewController.m:154-160`). Otherwise the page must hold the alert form (LOT-036) with a
+    /// `raison` textarea, a non-empty `hash_check`, which is recorded in the session, and an action naming the same
+    /// message.
+    /// - Throws: `invalidLink`, `notLoggedIn`, `formUnavailable`, `network`.
+    public func prepare(link: URL, in session: HFRSession) async throws(ModeratorAlertError) -> ModeratorAlertPage {
+        try await prepare(link: link, through: session)
+    }
+
+    /// Posts `form` with `reason` in `raison`, line breaks as CRLF like a browser (legacy: `\n` → `\r\n`,
+    /// `AlerteModoViewController.m:210`).
+    ///
+    /// Every answer HFR gives with a sentence comes back as `ModeratorAlertAnswer`, whether LOT-037 would read it as a
+    /// refusal or not: HFR's success page has a back link (`W46`), so it would otherwise read as a refusal and invite a
+    /// second alert (its reading is #395). Only HFR's logged-out sentence (`W17c`) is read: it is `notLoggedIn`.
+    /// - Throws: `emptyReason`, `unsupportedCharacters`, `unsupportedForm`, `sessionChanged` before sending; `network` when the request
+    ///   could not be sent; `notLoggedIn`; `unconfirmed` when the request may have left and no sentence was read.
+    public func submit(reason: String, with form: ModeratorAlertForm) async throws(ModeratorAlertError) -> ModeratorAlertAnswer {
+        guard !reason.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else { throw .emptyReason }
+        let refused = PostCharacterCheck.truncatingCharacters(in: reason)
+        guard refused.isEmpty else { throw .unsupportedCharacters(refused) }
+        let body: FormBody
+        do throws(PostingError) {
+            body = try PostingBody.make(
+                form: form.form, layout: form.layout, text: reason, textField: Self.reasonField, requiredFields: [Self.tokenField]
+            )
+        } catch .unsupportedForm(let cause) {
+            throw .unsupportedForm(reason: cause)
+        } catch {
+            // Not reached: `PostingBody.make` throws only `unsupportedForm`; the typed catch must still be exhaustive.
+            throw .unsupportedForm(reason: "body")
+        }
+        try await Self.checkBeforeSending(form)
